title: Three orders: compare Isolated and ChangeSet
scenario: A and C can be approved. B has an invalid delivery date. Compare two independent runs from the same initial data.
goal: Separate the HTTP batch envelope from the changeset rollback boundary.

steps.title: Select A, B and C
steps.explanation: Select all three and press Approve. No database result exists yet.
steps.outcome: One UI selection does not define one transaction.

steps.title: Run 1: isolated groups
steps.explanation: With #ISOLATED, each order has its own changeset. They can still share one $batch envelope.
steps.outcome: One HTTP request can carry independent outcomes.

steps.title: B fails; A and C succeed
steps.explanation: The date check rejects B. Its failure does not require rollback of the two independent successful changesets.
steps.outcome: Partial success is possible with independent changesets.

steps.title: Run 2: start again, one group
steps.explanation: Reset to the original unsaved data and use #CHANGE_SET. The three actions now belong to one changeset in this supported scenario.
steps.outcome: The rollback boundary now includes all three orders.

steps.title: One rejection stops the group
steps.explanation: B fails again. None of the approvals from this shared changeset is committed. Correct B or choose a different intended grouping.
steps.outcome: Verify persisted data, not just a successful HTTP response for the batch envelope.

takeaway: $batch groups transport. A changeset groups the atomic local outcome.
limitation: Illustrative supported Fiori elements service, not a live SAP execution. Actual request layout depends on the client and service version. Remote commits are outside this rollback boundary.
